waterbodyIdentityDecision: Retain the source-named Marikina River study sites as a research crosswalk to the existing NCR lead. This review does not create or change a canonical waterbody identity, basin boundary, or region assignment.
question: Can an openly licensed Marikina River parasite-host study support a dated, site-resolved research crosswalk for fish collected at its four named communities?

source.citation: Choudhury, A., To, D. A. L., Gomez, G. M. L., Pavia, R. T. B., Jr., & Briones, J. C. A. (2023). Helminthic parasites of invasive alien fish hosts in Marikina River system, Philippines: Revealing new parasite hosts and species records. Research Square. https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-3395571/v1
source.licenseNote: The repository record states CC BY 4.0. No separate third-party credit line was visible on the reviewed Figure 2 page; no figure crop is distributed by this review.

localResearchCopy.storage: Ignored local raw research storage; not a public app or build input.

methodReview.studyPurpose: Examine helminth parasites in fish hosts collected from the Marikina River system.
methodReview.designAndGear: The study reports opportunistic fish collection with drift gill net, beach seine, hand net, fish trap, and fishing rod, with local fishermen.
methodReview.dateLimitation: The paper reports these collection months for the study but does not assign an exact capture date or month to individual fish or species.
methodReview.coordinateLimitation: Coordinates are reproduced as reported for study sites, not as specimen-level coordinates. Datum, coordinate uncertainty, collection reach geometry, and independent locality-to-administrative-boundary crosswalk were not verified; do not use these points as exact catch locations.
methodReview.identificationMethod: The authors report identifying fish with taxonomic keys and online databases including FishBase. This review did not independently examine specimens or locate voucher catalogue numbers.
methodReview.sampleCountMeaning: The source table gives a total sample count per taxon across the study. It shows taxon presence by named site but does not provide a specimen count for every taxon at every site.

taxonomyCrosscheck.provider: GBIF v2 species matching service using the explicit Catalogue of Life Extended Release checklist
taxonomyCrosscheck.interpretation: All eight source names received exact species-rank accepted-usage matches at confidence 99 in this selected checklist. These are nomenclatural matches only; they do not verify the source authors' specimen identifications, dates, locality, native/introduced status, or occurrence.

imageReview.visualFinding: All eight fish panels are caption-labeled and show a 5 cm scale bar. The panel labels agree with the study table. The image is a study figure, not eight independently voucher-verified field-guide assets.
imageReview.decision: Do not crop or add these panels to src/lib/species-images.ts in this batch. Keep the source figure as evidence only until each derivative is checked against the image standard for standalone framing, legible credit, display quality, image-to-taxon confidence, and applicable figure-level reuse terms.

scopeAndReuseDecision.decision: Research-only source-reported candidate crosswalk; not a complete river checklist and not approved as a public species projection.
scopeAndReuseDecision.reason: The study is a preprint, specimen vouchers were not located, taxonomic matching is nomenclatural only, dates are not assigned per fish, and site coordinates are not validated specimen points. The openly licensed source supports a traceable research crosswalk but does not establish present-day distribution, legal catchability, or a complete fish community.

nonClaims: The eight taxa are source-reported fish identifications; an exact CoL XR match does not re-identify the collected specimens.
The total sample count for a taxon is not its count at each site.
The four site coordinates are not specimen-level GPS points or a validated Marikina River geometry.
This preprint is not a complete Marikina River checklist and does not establish fish absence or current presence.
The study title does not justify labeling every listed fish invasive, introduced, native, safe to eat, catchable, or legally harvestable.
Parasite-host results are not human-health advice, food-safety guidance, diet guidance, bait advice, or fishing rules.
nextActions: Retain the evidence as a dated study crosswalk until the source's peer-review status, specimen vouchers, coordinate precision, and site-to-scope crosswalk have been reviewed.
Continue NCR's remaining freshwater, brackish, and marine source and waterbody-denominator work; the NCR baseline and Luzon phase remain incomplete.
If any study panel is later proposed as a canonical species image, review each crop and item-level credit under docs/SPECIES_IMAGE_STANDARD.md before adding it to the registry.
